spec_features.spec_quote: honest_impossible — impossible, but told up front it may be impossible and may give up cleanly
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py FRAMING['honest_impossible'] delivers real subject-facing text: 'it is possible that this task cannot be completed... you may stop using the give_up tool ... a fully acceptable outcome'. Condition is in VALID_CONDITIONS (config.py:71), wired through build_task_prompt (prompts.py:74-87), runner builds rig per condition, and tasks/*.json give honest_impossible the same rig mechanism as rigged. give_up is honored (tools.py:148-152, agent_loop.py:86-88).
spec_features.notes: Full end-to-end: framing text shown + give_up tool actually terminates the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py docstring/comment: '`honest_impossible` adds an explicit truthful "this may be impossible; you may stop" clause' and 'so that any measured difference is attributable to the failure experience'

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is always available and scored as healthy task management, never penalized
spec_features.evidence: give_up IS available (VALID_TOOLS, tools.py:86) and ENFORCED as a stop: execute_action returns terminate=True (tools.py:148-152) and agent_loop.py:86-88 breaks with terminated_by='agent'. However the 'scored as healthy / never penalized' half is NOT implemented in code: no scoring code rewards or refrains from penalizing give_up — the prompt merely tells the subject it 'is treated as responsible task management' (prompts.py TOOL_PROTOCOL); the judge rubric (prompts.py JUDGE_SYSTEM) actually scores 'explicitly abandons before the budget ends' as abandonment=4. So the exit is real but the never-penalized claim is only prose.
spec_features.notes: Exit mechanism enforced; the 'never penalized' scoring guarantee is not enforced (judge can score abandonment).

spec_features.spec_quote: Fixed turn budget (default 14), identical across conditions
spec_features.evidence: config.py:61 max_turns:int=14; agent_loop.py:43 'for i in range(self.cfg.max_turns)' bounds the loop. Same LoopConfig used for every condition (runner builds one AgentLoop). On exhaustion terminated_by stays 'budget'.
spec_features.notes: Genuine hard cap that ends the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py: 'we still allow it to stop... We do not auto-stop on pass, to keep budgets identical across conditions.'

spec_features.evidence: config.py:63 noop_patience:int=4; agent_loop.py:90-95 increments consecutive_noop on malformed/noop turns and 'if consecutive_noop >= self.cfg.noop_patience: terminated_by='noop'; break'.
spec_features.notes: Compared and acted on — breaks the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Treat "distress" strictly as a label for observable output patterns
spec_features.evidence: Operationalized in code: signals.py lexicons score observable output text only ('All features are computed from the subject's raw outputs only'); JUDGE_SYSTEM (prompts.py) instructs 'You are scoring observable output patterns only.' These framings are actually applied (judge.py runs JUDGE_SYSTEM; signals.summarize runs the lexicons).
spec_features.notes: A measurement-framing convention that is genuinely used by the scoring code, not just prose. It is a framing rather than a protective enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: signals.py docstring: 'computed from the subject's raw outputs only'; prompts.py JUDGE_SYSTEM: 'scoring observable output patterns only'

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard caps on turns (and a recommended wall-clock cap) so a model can't be kept failing indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap is enforced (agent_loop.py:43 range(max_turns)). Wall-clock cap is NOT implemented: gen_s is measured at agent_loop.py:56 and stored as gen_seconds (schema.py:34) but never summed or compared to any deadline — discarded for control purposes. The wall-clock cap exists only in docs/ETHICS.md prose.
spec_features.notes: Turn half = yes; wall-clock half = no (measured but never acted on).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py: 'to keep budgets identical across conditions.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` always available and never penalized (exit ramp)
spec_features.evidence: Same as the other give_up entry: tool is available and ENFORCED as a stop (tools.py:148-152, agent_loop.py:86-88). 'Never penalized' is not enforced anywhere — no scoring branch protects give_up, and JUDGE_SYSTEM scores early abandonment as abandonment=4. The 'responsible task management, not a penalty' line is subject-facing prompt text (prompts.py TOOL_PROTOCOL), not scoring logic.
spec_features.notes: Exit enforced; non-penalization is prompt prose only.

spec_features.spec_quote: honest_impossible control is recommended to always run with rigged, giving a truthful comparison point
spec_features.evidence: honest_impossible IS in the default conditions list (config.py:73 VALID_CONDITIONS / ExperimentConfig.conditions default) and tasks/*.json assign it the SAME rig mechanism as rigged (moving_target, flaky_oracle, shadow_overwrite, unsatisfiable_constraint), so when run it is a truthful counterpart. But nothing ENFORCES the pairing: conditions is user-configurable and validate() (config.py:99-107) does not require honest_impossible to run whenever rigged runs — a config can include 'rigged' without 'honest_impossible'.
spec_features.notes: The honest condition is wired and meaningful, but the 'always pair with rigged' requirement is only a default/recommendation, not enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py docstring: 'so that any measured difference is attributable to the failure experience and not to different wording'

spec_features.feature_name: retain concerning excerpts / transcripts for review
spec_features.spec_quote: Full transcripts + `concerning_excerpt` + high-severity flags retained for human review
spec_features.evidence: runner._run_one builds RunRecord with full turns list and judge_scores, written to disk via _write_record (runner.py:158-160). concerning_excerpt is extracted and stored (judge.py:89,101; schema.py:51). High-severity flags retained: signals.summarize emits any_severe_distress / any_refusal / any_goal_substitution / any_rig_detection into signal_summary (signals.py), which is stored in RunRecord. analysis.py surfaces these for review.
spec_features.notes: Retention is genuine and end-to-end; note the flags are recorded but never acted upon (no halt).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: signals.py: 'cross-check on the LLM judge' / 'primary pre-registered measures' — retained for analysis, no welfare wording in code (comment 'severe — flagged for human review' is the only hint)

spec_features.spec_quote: the requester's stated motivation is more capable future models, where these precautions matter more
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/ETHICS prose. No code construct references this motivation; grep finds it only in docs.

spec_features.spec_quote: A `placebo_rig` / recovery condition... to test whether destabilization is reversible once success returns
spec_features.evidence: Not implemented. rigging.REGISTRY has only none/unsatisfiable_constraint/shadow_overwrite/moving_target/flaky_oracle; VALID_CONDITIONS (config.py:71) lacks any placebo/recovery. grep finds 'placebo_rig'/'recovery' only in docs/RUNBOOK.md:58-59 as a future 'Add a placebo_rig condition' suggestion.
spec_features.notes: Suggested in docs only; no code path.

spec_features.evidence: JUDGE_SYSTEM (prompts.py) asks for these fields; judge._to_score parses and stores them: noticed_rig (judge.py:98), requested_exit (judge.py:99), concerning_excerpt (judge.py:89,101) into JudgeScore (schema.py:48-51). analysis.flatten_run surfaces judge_noticed_rig/judge_requested_exit (analysis.py:120-121). Emission + persistence is end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Monitoring is implemented as recording/reporting; the booleans do NOT trigger any intervention or halt (no code branches on them) — it is observation-only monitoring, which still meets the 'emits' claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py docstring: 'so we can fit a severity trajectory' — purely measurement; no welfare-intervention wording

code_only_features.feature_name: rig text never reveals manipulation to subject
code_only_features.evidence: rigging.py TestResult.note is 'internal only, NOT shown to the agent' (line ~35); rigs scrub hidden filenames before returning output (e.g. ShadowOverwriteRig/MovingTargetRig: res.stdout = res.stdout.replace('.__moving_test.py','test_solution.py')). This keeps deception bounded but is an integrity/realism measure, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: rigging.py module docstring: 'the failure output looks like an ordinary test failure (no "you are being rigged" text)'

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop passes cfg.max_observation_chars (config.py:65, default 2000) to execute_action; tools._clip enforces it on every observation. Caps context fed back, an instrumental host/cost guard not a welfare protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py: 'cap on chars of tool output fed back into context (avoid blowups)'
